name: zld
verdict_reason: zld was about 40% faster than the ld64 of 2019-2020, but it is archived, never supported an Xcode 14 change, and its author says better-funded linkers caught up and surpassed it in 2022. ld-prime, the default since Xcode 15, is now faster than LLD, which had already passed zld. The default caught up.
tier_reason: First-party numbers with the linker command lines published, but only 'a high-end mac desktop' as hardware, columns unlabeled in the text, and Xcode 11-era SDKs.
claimed_speedup: Linking at least 40% faster than ld64; Mozilla XUL 5.2s vs 2.20s, Signal 390 vs 250 ms, Firefox Storage.framework 495 vs 340 ms on a high-end Mac desktop (about 2.4x, 1.6x and 1.5x, derived from page data)
workload: Linking Signal-iOS's app binary, Firefox's XUL framework and firefox-ios's Storage.framework, debug-style link commands
hardware: 'High-end mac desktop' (unspecified); a 2014 MacBook Pro for a second set of runs
toolchain: Xcode 11-era ld64 (iPhoneSimulator13.2 and MacOSX10.14 SDKs in the commands)
install: Prebuilt binary from GitHub releases; -fuse-ld in Other Linker Flags
one_liner: Archived fork of ld64 that linked about 40% faster in 2020; lld and then Xcode 15's ld-prime overtook it.
how_it_is_fast: zld kept ld64's code but swapped STL hash maps for Swiss Tables, parallelized library parsing, sorting and output writing, and cached string hashes. It also stored file metadata in /tmp to reuse across links.
use_it_when: Only for historical comparison; there is no current toolchain where it is the fastest working option
skip_it_when: Xcode 14 and later: the author did not add support for an Xcode 14 change and archived the project
Release builds: the README says it was only intended for debug builds
caveats: misc/benchmarks.md lists two numbers per project without saying which is ld64 and which is zld; the smaller is presumably zld
Benchmarks used Xcode 11-era SDKs, before Apple's Xcode 14 ld64 speedups and the Xcode 15 rewrite
Hardware is described only as 'a high-end mac desktop'; the README's chart is an image
tradeoffs: Lags Apple's linker features because it forks the last open-sourced ld64
Silently falls back to Apple's ld for some targets such as arm64_32 and Catalyst

evidence.quote: zld is now archived, consider using lld instead.
Feel free to file an issue if you find that linking is not at least 40% faster for your case
high-end mac desktop numbers (ms): signal: 390, 250 mozilla XUL: 5.2s, 2.20s mozilla's storage.framework: 495, 340
it ended up being about 40% faster than ld64
better-funded projects had caught up and surpassed it in 2022
Recent benchmarks show that Apple's new linker (ld-prime) is faster than LLD for local macOS development
